title: Make "Archive all" move the messages

blocks.text: The mail client keeps each folder as a list of messages, and each screen redraws from the list it holds. The folder operations in `Folders` take those lists and change them: `deleteFrom` already works, and the inbox screen shows the result as soon as it returns.

"Archive all" is not written yet. Finish `archiveAll(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/Folders.java`. When you're done, the inbox screen shows an empty inbox, the archive screen shows the moved messages after the ones it already had (also when the archive was empty), and the method returns how many messages moved. About three lines in total.

cases.says: archiveAll returns the number of messages the inbox held
the inbox list the caller passed is empty after the call
the archive list the caller passed holds its own messages followed by the inbox's, in order
an archive list that was empty receives the inbox's messages as well

origin.section: Java Copies Every Argument, So Assigning to a Parameter Never Reaches the Caller's Variable

concepts: A parameter is a new variable holding a copy of the argument's value, so assigning to it, primitive or reference, never changes the caller's variable, while a call through the copied reference changes the caller's object.
After a method assigns a new object to its parameter, every later change through that parameter goes to the new object, not to the caller's.
